context.concept_name: Service release and rollback workflow with build, release and run separation

coverage.learning_objective: Separate build release and run: specify one release/rollback procedure.

required_facts.statement: Build creates an executable artifact, release combines that artifact with deploy-specific configuration, and run starts processes from the selected release.
Releases have unique identifiers and are immutable; a new change produces a new release rather than mutating a running release.
Record the artifact and configuration for each release and define rollback by redeploying a known prior release with its intended configuration.
Check the prior release's compatibility with the current database schema before selecting it for rollback; replacing an application release does not itself reverse a database migration.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: Rolling back an application means selecting a known release, but the database may have changed since that release ran. Artifact replacement and schema reversal are different boundaries.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Build creates an executable artifact, release combines that artifact with deploy-specific configuration, and run starts processes from the selected release.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Releases have unique identifiers and are immutable; a new change produces a new release rather than mutating a running release. Record the artifact and configuration for each release and define rollback by redeploying a known prior release with its intended configuration. Check the prior release's compatibility with the current database schema before selecting it for rollback; replacing an application release does not itself reverse a database migration.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Record the executable artifact and deploy-specific configuration under a unique immutable release identifier. Build creates the artifact, release combines it with configuration, and run starts the selected release's processes. A later change creates a new release instead of mutating the running one. For rollback, identify a known prior release with its intended configuration and check compatibility with the current database schema before redeployment. Trace the release record and database schema independently: selecting old application code does not automatically reverse a migration. This makes rollback a concrete deployment selection supported by compatibility evidence, not a vague instruction to replace files until the old behavior appears.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: Application rollback does not itself undo database migrations. Verify the prior release against the current schema.

coverage.learning_objective: Recognize N+1 access: remove one N+1 listing read.

required_facts.statement: Lazy relationship access can emit additional SELECT statements; iterating parent entities and loading each parent's relationship separately can produce an N+1 query pattern.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary

segments.label: Replace per-movie review queries with selectinload
segments.summary: Accessing a movie's reviews can issue a separate SELECT because the relationship is loaded lazily. Listing eight movies and accessing each collection produces nine queries: one for the movies and eight for their reviews. With engine echo logging enabled, the demonstration exposes these repeated queries, then imports selectinload from sqlalchemy.orm and adds options(selectinload(Movie.reviews)) to the statement. The resulting SQL retrieves the movies first, then fetches their reviews together using the selected movie IDs in an IN clause. For this listing, the query count falls from nine to two without introducing a join. The demonstration uses synchronous session execution.

context.concept_name: Authentication and authorization tests including invalid-token rejection

coverage.learning_objective: Verify API authentication and authorization rejection: test one protected resource with invalid, insufficient and valid credentials.

required_facts.statement: Send requests through the real protected HTTP endpoint with absent, malformed and supplied bearer credentials, keeping the authentication and verification gates active.
Test invalid-signature, expired and contextually wrong tokens separately from a valid token, asserting credential rejection before protected output is returned.
Test an otherwise valid credential lacking the required permission separately from a valid sufficiently permitted credential to distinguish authentication from operation authorization.
Test a valid caller against another caller's object identifier as a separate deny path from missing operation permission.
Assert the declared status and safe body for each denial and the public projected result for the fully authorized request, not merely that some requests fail and one succeeds.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A protected order endpoint needs tests of distinct denial gates as well as full success. One rejected request does not prove every security boundary works.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Send requests through the real protected HTTP endpoint with absent, malformed and supplied bearer credentials, keeping the authentication and verification gates active.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Test invalid-signature, expired and contextually wrong tokens separately from a valid token, asserting credential rejection before protected output is returned. Test an otherwise valid credential lacking the required permission separately from a valid sufficiently permitted credential to distinguish authentication from operation authorization. Test a valid caller against another caller's object identifier as a separate deny path from missing operation permission. Assert the declared status and safe body for each denial and the public projected result for the fully authorized request, not merely that some requests fail and one succeeds.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Exercise the real endpoint with absent, malformed and supplied bearer credentials while keeping extraction and verification active. Separate invalid signature, expiry and wrong token context from a valid credential. Next use a valid credential lacking operation permission, then a valid caller requesting another caller's object. These isolate authentication, operation authorization and object authorization. Finally send a fully authorized request and assert the public projected result. For every denial, assert declared status and safe body before protected output is returned. Label each test by the gate it proves, not merely "fails." Substituting away verification would weaken the evidence precisely where this exercise requires real rejection behavior.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: One denial plus one success is not complete security coverage. Isolate each credential and authorization failure while real gates remain active.

video_need.reason: Running controlled success and failure cases makes the observable application boundary and assertions concrete. Focus: Verify API authentication and authorization rejection: test one protected resource with invalid, insufficient and valid credentials.

practice_anchor.objective: Test one protected order endpoint through real HTTP requests with absent, malformed, invalid-signature, expired, wrong-context, insufficient-permission and fully authorized credentials. Include a separately tested request for another caller's order.
practice_anchor.success: Each credential rejection, missing-permission denial and cross-object denial has its own test asserting the declared status and safe body without protected output. The fully authorized request returns the expected public projection, with authentication and verification active throughout.
